desc: Derive and verify the combinatorial count: pairs of pieces in a given unordered pair of rows = n² · C(mn−2, k−2); confirmed with examples (m=n=2,k=2 → 8; m=1,n=4,k=3 → 20).
Obtain closed form for unordered-pair distance sum Σ_{r1<r2} |r1−r2| = (m³−m)/6; division handled via modular inverse of 6.

Implement the full solution: factorial-based C(N−2, k−2) mod p, final formula ans = C(N−2,k−2) · (n²·(m³−m) + m²·(n³−n)) · inv(6) mod (1e9+7); verified against both examples and 2×3 brute force (k=2 → 25, k=3 → 100).
Test edge cases: k = 2, k = m·n, m = 1 or n = 1, and large m·n near 10⁵ for performance; brute-force cross-check on additional small grids (3×3, k=2,4 → 72 and 1512, all matching formula).
